NDT training in Brownsville, TX: how it works

Short answer: Brownsville and Rio Grande Valley technicians take NDT theory self-paced on the Atlantis online portal, where an ASNT NDT Level III answers questions, and access opens as soon as you enroll. You rehearse in the Practical NDT browser simulator and complete hands-on training and the practical exam in person at your employer's facility. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Brownsville. The employer certifies you under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, or you take ASNT central exams.

Brownsville has become one of the fastest-changing inspection markets in Texas. For decades the Port of Brownsville was known for cargo, ship recycling and a shipyard that built and repaired offshore rigs. Now it also hosts a large LNG export plant under construction, with a second export project in development, and SpaceX's Starbase sits on the coast to the east. Construction on this scale brings a surge in weld inspection: visual, magnetic particle and penetrant on structural and piping welds, and radiography or ultrasonic examination of pressure piping and tanks.

For a local technician, that creates a real opportunity to enter the trade, as long as the training leads to certification an employer can stand behind. Theory comes first and is self-paced on the portal. The practical skill is built by working under a certified Level II or III at a Valley employer or contractor. The employer's written practice, examinations and signature complete the process.

Tell us what Brownsville training you need: methods, levels and the number of trainees. We reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Brownsville: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Most contractors working at the port and on the LNG projects certify technicians to written practices based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Whether you are new to the trade or moving over from welding or fitting, the steps run in this order.

  1. Identify the written practice. It belongs to the company that will certify you and sets the training hours, experience hours, exams and vision requirements for each method. To gauge your own starting point, try the eligibility tool.
  2. Complete the training hours for the method and level online. The SNT-TC-1A hours planner shows recommended minimums by method.
  3. Work under supervision on real welds and equipment, with a certified Level II or III signing your experience log.
  4. Pass a general exam on the method's principles, instruments and vocabulary.
  5. Pass a specific exam on the employer's procedures and the acceptance criteria in the project specification, which on LNG work cite codes such as ASME B31.3.
  6. Pass a practical exam on specimens containing known discontinuities, graded by or under a Level III.
  7. Pass the eye tests for near vision and color contrast that the written practice calls for.
  8. Get your employer's certification, signed and kept on file by the company.
  9. Stay current with recertification at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should be no more than five years.

ASNT central certification, ASNT 9712 for Level I and II or the ASNT NDT Level III examinations, is the option if you want a credential that is not tied to one contractor, and Atlantis prepares candidates for it. The employer route is explained in more depth on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Brownsville technicians

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. Newcomers usually start with Level 1 NDT training, add Level 2 as their experience grows and consider ASNT Level III training later. The table links each method to work around the port.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Brownsville
VTVisual acuity, lighting and access, weld gauges, fit-up and visual acceptance criteriaEvery structural, piping and tank weld on the LNG projects and at port fabricators
MTYoke technique, field direction, particle types and interpretationCarbon steel structural and piping welds, pipe supports, lifting points and cranes
PTPre-cleaning, penetrant dwell, removal, developer and evaluationStainless and cryogenic piping welds, non-magnetic valves and fittings
RTExposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital radiography, interpretationProcess and pressure piping welds during construction, repair welds
UTCalibration, thickness gauging, angle-beam weld examination and reportingWeld examination on piping and structural steel, thickness surveys on vessels, hulls and terminal equipment
PAUT and TOFDPhased-array setups, encoded scanning, TOFD, data analysis and sizing for UT Level II techniciansLarge-bore and thick-wall welds on project work where the owner and code allow ultrasonic examination
ETImpedance-plane displays, probe selection and surface techniquesSurface crack detection through coatings, and heat-exchanger tubing in operating plants

Level III preparation suits a Valley technician who already supervises a crew and wants to move into procedure writing and examination. It covers the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and gives practice drafting procedures and exams.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Brownsville

As the LNG plants and their piping go in, more of the volumetric examination of welds is being done ultrasonically, alongside radiography. Ultrasonic examination avoids the radiation exclusion zones that slow other trades on a crowded construction site, which is why owners and contractors often prefer it where the code permits. The ultrasonic testing training course builds the foundation: sound physics, calibration, angle-beam scanning of butt welds, sizing and clear reporting.

The method used most around Brownsville right now, though, is visual inspection, closely followed by MT and PT. Every weld on a construction project is visually inspected first, and surface methods catch cracks and other open defects on structural and piping welds. Someone entering the trade in the Valley will usually be most employable with VT, MT and PT certifications first, then UT or RT.

Where NDT technicians work around Brownsville

LNG export construction. NextDecade's Rio Grande LNG is being built at the Port of Brownsville, with Bechtel as the engineering, procurement and construction contractor and five liquefaction trains in progress. A second export project, Texas LNG, is in development at the port. Projects like these employ large numbers of NDT technicians through construction contractors and inspection companies, mostly in VT, MT, PT, RT and UT.

Shipyard and marine work. The port's large shipyard has built and repaired offshore rigs and vessels for decades; in 2025 Seatrium agreed to sell its AmFELS yard there to an affiliate of Karpowership. Marine construction and repair need hull and structural weld inspection and thickness surveys.

Ship recycling. Brownsville is home to some of the main ship recycling yards in the United States, where retired naval and commercial vessels are dismantled. Recycling work relies more on cutting and environmental controls than on NDT, but the yards and the scrap and steel trades around them add to the port's industrial base.

Aerospace at Boca Chica. SpaceX builds and launches Starship vehicles at its Starbase site east of Brownsville. Rocket production follows the company's own quality requirements and staffing, and the activity has drawn welding, fabrication and supplier work to the area.

Terminals, pipelines and cross-border trade. Fuel and bulk terminals along the ship channel, the pipelines that feed them and manufacturing tied to Matamoros across the border all need periodic inspection of tanks, piping and structural steel.

Public earnings data is gathered in the NDT salary guide.

NDT schools and classes near Brownsville: what to compare

Search for NDT classes in the Rio Grande Valley and you will find community college welding and industrial programs, schools further up the coast, and online courses that pair self-paced theory with a practical at an employer. Before you commit, check that the training will meet the written practice of the contractor you want to work for.

  • Which standard does the course follow, and does the completion record list method, level and hours clearly?
  • Who is the Level III behind the course, and which methods does that person hold?
  • How is hands-on training provided, and will you work on welded specimens like the ones on the LNG and port projects?
  • Is the course aimed at employer certification, an ASNT central examination, or both?
  • What record do you keep if you move from one project contractor to the next?

Our answer is self-paced theory on the portal with Level III Q&A, simulator practice in the browser, and the hands-on practical and practical examination in person at the employer's facility under its written practice. The published US fees for each course are in the table on this page, and Register & Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal. Common follow-up questions are on the NDT training FAQ.

Online NDT training in Texas

Construction work on the Valley's big projects often means long days and changing shifts. Self-paced theory fits that: on the Atlantis portal you study whenever you can, revisit difficult topics and send questions to the Level III. You never have to be online at a set time.

The practical side still has to be done in person. Texas employers certify after supervised hands-on experience and a practical examination on real parts. For more on the state, see NDT training in Texas and the Gulf Coast page; the US overview is at NDT training in the USA.

Training a crew at your Brownsville facility (employers)

When a contractor mobilizes to Brownsville and needs local hires qualified, the efficient pattern is theory online for the whole group, followed by hands-on training and practical examinations in person at the contractor's site on its own equipment and weld samples. The specific examination is written around the project specification and the contractor's procedures, so the crew is tested on what it will actually inspect.

Large projects audit their contractors' certification files closely. Written practice development makes sure your program document covers every method and technique you will use on the job, and outsourced ASNT Level III consulting can review procedures, prepare and grade examinations and audit technician files before the owner does. Group training is described on the corporate NDT training page.

Radiography licensing in Texas

As an NRC Agreement State, Texas licenses industrial radiography through its own Radiation Control Program at the Department of State Health Services. Companies using sources or industrial X-ray equipment hold a state license under 25 TAC §289.255, and every person who operates the equipment must hold a Texas industrial radiographer certification or a reciprocal certification the state accepts. That requires a radiation safety course, supervised experience as a trainee and a state examination.

An NDT method course does not provide that certification. Radiographic testing training covers exposure technique and interpretation for SNT-TC-1A certification, while radiation safety certification runs through the employer's licensed program and the state. On Brownsville construction sites, radiographers carry both. Check DSHS's current requirements before planning a radiography career.

Practice before your practical exam

Practical NDT runs in a browser and lets you rehearse inspections before your practical. For construction work around the port, the welding workshop, the visual testing simulator and the radiography simulator are good places to start. Simulator practice builds confidence, but it does not count as logged experience and does not replace the practical examination on real welds.

The free NDT practice tests help you check your theory method by method.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Brownsville

How long does it take to get NDT certified in Brownsville?

Your employer's written practice sets it. The theory can be finished in a few weeks of steady work; the supervised experience hours usually take several months per level.

How much does NDT training cost in the Rio Grande Valley?

The published US fees for each course appear in the table on this page. Contractors training a group can contact us, and we reply within one business day.

Can I learn NDT online from Brownsville?

Yes, the theory is online and self-paced. The hands-on practical and the practical examination take place in person at the employer.

Is there an NDT school near me in Brownsville?

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Brownsville or elsewhere in the Valley. Theory is online and practical work happens at your employer's facility. Compare any school using the checklist above.

What NDT method should I start with for LNG construction?

VT, then MT and PT. Those cover most weld inspection on structural and piping work. RT or UT come next as your experience grows.

Are there NDT jobs in Brownsville?

The LNG construction projects, port fabricators and shipyard work, terminals and pipelines all create NDT jobs, mostly through construction and inspection contractors. Demand follows project schedules.

I am a welder. Can I move into NDT?

Yes, and welding experience helps, especially for VT. You still need the training hours, supervised experience and examinations in your new employer's written practice. Some employers also look for AWS CWI for welding inspection roles, which is a separate credential.

Does my certification transfer when I change contractors?

Not automatically. Each employer certifies you under its own written practice after reviewing your records. ASNT central certification stays with you.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Brownsville?

Yes, the Level III course is self-paced online with questions answered by the instructor.

Who teaches the courses?

Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international NDT field experience.
